groups.checked_reason: X is compact complex; Y is connected compact of dimension r>=1, theta smooth real (1,1), omega Hermitian and generic ambient Lelong number zero. This setup now precedes the symbol-bearing motivation.
The restricted-analytic bound makes u_m|Y nontrivial; image ideals remain coherent and nonzero on compact models and give finitely many divisorial components at each m.
Generic pole coefficients b_m(E)/m are removed from theta_Z+epsilon_m omega_Z^0+ddc w_m using the nonclosed divisorial removal lemma.
Integration by parts kills dd c w_m against gamma^(r-1); fixed pulled-back smooth backgrounds are finite and epsilon_m tends to zero, including r=1.

groups.topic: Countability of the infinite divisorial sum
groups.checked_reason: Every prime divisor has positive gamma area. Only finitely many terms can have mass >=1/k, yielding countability and a summable positive mass budget.
Increasing finite positive closed partial sums with bounded coefficient measures converge weakly to a positive finite-mass current; differentiation preserves closedness.
Coefficient convergence dominated by the summable trace series yields vanishing positive-tail mass and weak convergence. Ideal superadditivity gives D_2m>=D_m.
Generic isomorphisms identify valuations; proper pushforward of summable positive currents preserves the coefficientwise compatibility.
Exceptional prime divisors map into codimension>=2 and test forms pull back to zero by rank <=r-2; smooth compact curve modifications are isomorphisms.
Normal local divisibility gives the image ideal inclusion. Orders along a fixed prime divisor on the higher model give finite coefficient bounds before m tends to infinity.

The earlier nonclosed restricted-analytic envelope gives one original-background potential on Y satisfying all trace inequalities; finite removal and positive limits dominate all S_Z. Exact realization requires a separate reverse inequality.
The earlier global-potential decomposition and smoothness of distributions with smooth dd c give surjectivity and injectivity of the natural cohomology map.
The trace pairing is cohomological; positivity and a strictly positive metric force zero representatives when the trace is zero, excluding lines in the cone.

groups.topic: Hopf Bott-Chern versus de Rham class
groups.checked_reason: d c log|z|^2 descends, giving de Rham exactness, while the earlier normalized Hopf calculation gives Gauduchon degree 2(n-1)>0.

The common majorant gives positive residual representatives in a closed ambient background. Pushforward compatibility and ideal equivalence preserve classes; nonclosed derivatives require the next affine chapter.
Local Bergman estimates bound normalized multiplier-ideal vanishing between max(nu_E-A_E/m,0) and nu_E. The limit equals nu_E, including zero coefficients.
Divisorial removal gives positive closed regular parts; degree-one pushforward and self-trace compatibility give the b-divisor relation and additivity.
The bounded almost-regularization result supplies smooth beta+dd c v_j>=-epsilon_j gamma; closedness of R implies beta closed, preserving the Bott-Chern class.

The book analytic-singularity convention has positive rational coefficient. Log resolution therefore gives a finite rational divisor and bounded residual potential; bounded pullbacks have zero Lelong numbers on higher models.
The normalized Gauduchon Green inverse acts on top-degree zero-total-mass distributions, producing linear distributionally continuous potentials and closed forms of constant trace.
For real (1,1) B, xi wedge B=0 forces a multiple of xi wedge Jxi; its trace is nonzero. The paired symbol is injective, including complex dimension one.
P*P is elliptic; its distributional kernel is finite-dimensional and smooth. Integration of its quadratic form identifies it with closed constant-trace forms.
Applying the normalized inverse to dd c f yields B=0; the scalar elliptic kernel and zero-mean normalization give uniqueness in each Bott-Chern class.
Smooth convergence of B gives one lower curvature bound. Normalized compactness and zero mean bound suprema, identify every L1 cluster point and bound norms on the compact unit-mass cone.

groups.topic: Modification pullback continuity and mass bound
groups.checked_reason: Earlier L1 pullback for qpsh potentials with one lower curvature bound gives weak continuity. Gauduchon integration reduces pulled-back mass to a fixed smooth representative norm.
Positive closed tails pull back additively with mass bounded by C_g times their original mass; local divisor equations and positive summability justify regrouping.

Finite partial pullbacks are dominated by S_Zprime; strict-transform coefficients agree. Only finitely many exceptional components remain. Local potentials make pullback functorial and give the effective cocycle.
The signed exceptional error is the difference of two positive tails. Their upstairs trace masses tend to zero by the linear pullback estimate.

Global logarithmic exceptional potentials exist; dd c of the remaining difference is smooth, so the difference is smooth. Almost-everywhere equality extends to qpsh representatives; generic Lelong numbers show equality of types iff E_g=0.

groups.topic: Residual class correction and exact trace realization
groups.checked_reason: The common envelope and smooth background pull back exactly, whereas subtracting the divisor current gives R_Zprime=g*R_Z-[E_g]. This does not obstruct exact realization by another potential.

A rational logarithmic point pole on P2 has no downstairs divisorial component and exceptional coefficient a after blowup. Its product with a BMP counterexample preserves exact analytic trace; smooth binomial expansion gives choose(k+2,2) times the divergent factor mass, and scaling establishes failure for C Omega.
